text.p: Morocco's leading Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur showed a net profit of 366 million dirhams ($38.9 million) in 1996, up 21 percent on the previous year, the weekly La Nouvelle Tribune newspaper said.
"BMCE results jumped 21.6 percent to 366 million dirhams in 1996 from 301 million dirhams in the previous year," the newspaper said.
Contacted by Reuters, a bank official said BMCE's audited consolidated balance sheet was expected to be published soon. He did not dispute the figure cited but declined any comment.

One of the largest market capitalisation companies, BMCE had a capital of 1.0 billion dirhams before a capital increase in May 1996. Then the new capital was set at 1.44 billion dirhams divided in 14.4 million shares of 100 dirhams nominal value each, a bourse official said.
BMCE's turnover rose in 1996 to 3.18 billion dirhams from 2.52 billion dirhams in 1995, the newspaper said. Total assets rose by 2.4 percent to 34.7 billion dirhams compared with 1995, it said.
One of the eight banks listed on the Casablanca stock exchange, BMCE was last traded at 495 dirhams, up from 400 dirhams at the beginning of the year, a stockbroker said.
The bank has a market capitalisation of more than 6.9 billion dirhams, the third largest after ONA Group and Banque Commerciale du Maroc, the broker added.
